newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz sees strong growth in 1996 pre-tax.
newsitem.headline: Allianz sees strong growth in 1996 pre-tax.

text.p: Europe's leading insurance group, Germany's Allianz AG Holding, said on Monday it expected to post strong growth in pre-tax earnings in 1996, although its net profit growth would be weaker.

"We expect another considerable improvement in pre-tax results, assuming that claims experience continues to be moderate, that we see no extraordinary catastrophes and that the current favourable situation on the capital markets does not drastically change," the group said in its interim report.
Allianz sees strong growth in 1996 pre =2

Allianz's pre-tax profit growth is expected to outstrip net profit because its net profit figure of 2.02 billion marks ($1.3 billion) in 1995 was boosted by tax breaks carried over from its east German unit, Deutsche Versicherungs AG.
The giant insurer's net profit rose 34.4 percent to 3.l04 billion marks in 1995.

In a speech at the company's annual shareholders' meeting on Monday, Allianz chairman Henning Schulte-Noelle said year-end earnings would be on a level "which will not endanger the dividend level of 16 marks."
The group said its premium income rose 8.3 percent to 39.6 billion marks in the first half of 1996 and that it expected a year-end rise in group premiums of around six percent.

That forecast excludes any possible consolidation effects from Allianz's final takeover of the Vereinte group and the Hermes loan insurance company and its sale of the DKV health insurance unit, which were announced earlier this year.
